text: Picture spacetime as fabric. Particles have spin, a quantum property like a compass arrow. In Einstein-Cartan gravity, an extension of Einstein's theory, spin gives that fabric a slight twist called torsion. The 2010 paper says that, at crushing density, torsion pushes back like a compressed spring. Collapse stops and reverses in a bounce. This paper contains no plots, the entire argument is equations, so our labeled graphic shows the spring-like turn. Its famous estimate says, today's torsion density is roughly a negative one, shifted 70 places past the decimal point. A whisper.
